segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: And here on Radio Rivenden we have Lynne Rawley, the .Public Relations Officer of our own Rivenden City Theatre.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Hello, Lynne.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Hello.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Now, the theatre is reopening soon after its three-year redevelopment programme, isn't it?

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: That's right, and there are a lot of improvements.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: The first thing people will see when they go in is that the foyer has been repainted in the original green and gold.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Then the box office has been reoriented. with its own access from the side of the building instead of through the foyer, which means it can be open longer hours, and has more space, too.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: The shop that used to be in the foyer, which sold books and CDs, is the one part of the redevelopment which isn't yet complete.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: The plan is to find new premises for it near the theatre, and we've had difficulty finding somewhere suitable.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: We hope to reopen the shop in the next few months.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Will audiences find any difference in the auditorium?

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Yes, we've increased the leg-room between the rows.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: This means that there are now fewer seats but we're sure audiences will be much happier.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: And we've installed air conditioning, so it won't get so hot and stuffy.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: We already had a few seats which were suitable for wheelchair users, and now there are twice as many, which we hope will meet demand.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Something else that will benefit audiences is the new lifts.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: The two we used to have were very small and slow.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: They've now gone. and we've got much more efficient ones.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Anything for the performers?

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Yes, we've made a number of improvements backstage.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: The small. dark dressing rooms we used to have have been converted into two large airy rooms, so they're much more comfortable now.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: And the state- of-the-art electronic sound and lighting systems have been installed.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK, so what's the first play that audiences can see when the theatre reopens?

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: We've got a very exciting production of Peter Shaffer's Royal Hunt of the Sun, which is currently touring the country.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: That starts on October the 13th and runs till the 19th.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: We're experimenting a bit with the time the curtain goes up.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: We used to start all our performances at 7.30, but that made it difficult for people to go home by public transport, so instead we're beginning at 1, because at 9.45, when it finishes, there are still buses running.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Tickets are already selling fast.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: The Friday and Saturday performances sold out almost immediately and, in fact, now there are only tickets for Monday and Thursday.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: How much are they?

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: We've introduced a simpler price structure.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: Ticket prices used to range fr~m £6 to £30 but now they're all ill.

segments.speaker: LYNNE
segments.en: They're available from the box office, in person, by phone, fax or post, or online.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK, Lynne, now if you'd like to give the contact details for the theatre ...
